stem: A person invests Rs 4000 at the end of each year for 3 years at 10% per annum compounded annually. What is the future value of these investments at the end of 3 years? [Given: (1.10)^2 = 1.21, (1.10)^3 = 1.331]

per_option_rationale.rationale: End-of-year ordinary annuity FV. Year 1 payment grows for 2 years: 4000*1.21 = 4840. Year 2 grows for 1 year: 4000*1.10 = 4400. Year 3 stays: 4000. Total = 4840 + 4400 + 4000 = Rs 13240.
Ignoring all interest on the deposits: 3 * 4000 = Rs 12000.

Treating the first payment as growing for 3 years instead of 2: 4000*1.331 + 4000*1.21 + 4000*1.10 = 5324 + 4840 + 4400 = 14564, or treating year 3 payment as growing for 1 year giving a different error; here off-by-one on counting periods gives 4000 * 1.331 + 4000 * 1.21 = 5324 + 4840 = 10164 then adding 4000 wrong to get 13310 if year 3 added at face value with (1.10)^3 by mistake.
Applying simple interest accumulation instead of compound: 4000*1.2 + 4000*1.1 + 4000 = 4800 + 4400 + 4000 = 13200.

explanation: For an ordinary annuity (payments at end of year), compound each payment to the end: first payment earns 2 years interest, second earns 1 year, third earns none. FV = 4000*(1.10)^2 + 4000*(1.10)^1 + 4000*(1.10)^0 = 4840 + 4400 + 4000 = Rs 13240.

explanation_sections.punchline: Each end-of-year payment grows for the remaining years, not for the full 3 years.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the model: ordinary annuity FV. Each payment PMT grows to PMT*(1+r)^k where k = years remaining. Sum: 4000*1.21 + 4000*1.10 + 4000 = 4840 + 4400 + 4000 = 13240.
explanation_sections.lesson: Payments at end of year grow for (n - t) years, not n years; the final payment earns no interest.
explanation_sections.timing: 60-70 seconds. Apply the hint values directly. Trap: if you use (1.10)^3 for the first payment you get 5324 and overshoot.
